drhp.business: Jaykay Enterprises manufactures precision-machined components, subassemblies, composite structures and underwater systems for Indian defence and aerospace programmes, largely through its step-down subsidiary Allen Reinforced Plastics. Its Digital Manufacturing arm does additive manufacturing, prototyping, powder metallurgy, reverse engineering and plant modelling, and has entered patient-specific and orthopaedic implants. Its material subsidiary J K Technosoft is a Gen AI-focused data services business serving Insurance & Financial Services and Retail & CPG clients through its JIVA AI orchestration platform, data transformation and cloud engineering.
drhp.end_markets: Indian defence and aerospace organisations (orders in FY26 from BrahMos Aerospace, Bharat Dynamics, HAL, BARC, BEL, NSTL, ADA)|Healthcare: orthopaedics and dental care (customised / patient-specific implants)|Enterprise IT clients in Insurance & Financial Services and Retail & CPG|United States and Europe (JIVA deployments for large enterprise customers)|Industrial sectors using additive manufacturing (aerospace, healthcare, automotive, energy, oil & gas)
drhp.expansion: JK Defence & Aerospace, a wholly owned subsidiary, is developing an Ultra Modern 400,000 sq ft advanced manufacturing complex at Devanahalli (North Bengaluru) for precision-turned components, systems and sub-systems for defence and aerospace: 200,000 sq ft precision manufacturing, a 100,000 sq ft Additive Manufacturing Center able to house 80-100 industrial 3D metal printers, about 50,000 sq ft of R&D and the balance offices. Civil construction is expected by December 2026 and project completion in Q4, 2027; a Rights Issue is underway primarily to fund it, and the project scope includes repaying interim loans taken by JK Defence for the facility. The Company funded JK Defence and JK Digital through subscriptions to 0.1% OCRPS during FY26 and the current year. In FY26 the Cherlapally (Hyderabad) facility expansion was completed, adding capability for large composite structures and advanced underwater systems, and the Peenya orthopaedic implant manufacturing project was completed, received CDSCO MD13 certification and began trial production. In April 2026 the Company acquired the Patange Industries business undertaking (defence precision manufacturing, fabrication and engineering design) by slump sale. JK Defence raised its stake in Allen Reinforced Plastics from 76.41% to 92.92% by paying call monies on rights shares, and the Company raised its stake in J K Technosoft to 99.07% (fully-converted basis) through a share swap.

litigation.note: Corporate Governance Report (non-compliances in last three years): SEBI order dated November 09, 2023 imposed a penalty on the Company for violations of SEBI Listing Regulations and SEBI (RTA) Regulations arising from an inspection of its former RTA activity. No other litigation evidence in this bundle.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Defence indigenisation (Atmanirbhar Bharat / Make in India), higher defence allocations, armed-forces modernisation and earmarking of procurement for indigenous manufacturers; management says JKE's capability indicates fitment with some ICDP / TPCR platforms and munitions.
- Growing private-sector participation in defence production and exports, and India's emergence as an aerospace manufacturing hub, raising demand for specialised precision, composite and systems-integration suppliers.
- Additive manufacturing shifting from prototyping to industrial production, supported by India's National Strategy for Additive Manufacturing.
- Healthcare as an emerging application for additive manufacturing: customised, patient-specific orthopaedic and dental implants.
- Enterprise adoption of Generative AI, Agentic AI, cloud, data engineering and hyper-automation driving IT services demand; JIVA seeing interest across Retail, Manufacturing, Consumer Products, Financial Services and Insurance.
- Consolidated revenue growth in FY26 attributed by the Board to the acquisition of J K Technosoft plus growth in the Defence & Digital manufacturing business.
- FY26 orders from strategic defence organisations including BrahMos Aerospace, Bharat Dynamics, HAL, BARC, BEL, NSTL and ADA; the Company participates in multiple development and qualification programs across missile systems, aerospace structures, defence electronics and underwater platforms.
- Allen received orders from BrahMos Aerospace Private Limited aggregating approximately Rs. 94.45 Crores (inclusive of GST) for Composite Parts.
- Allen received orders from Bharat Dynamics Limited aggregating approximately Rs. 15.90 Crores (inclusive of GST) for Launcher Tubes & Packing Boxes.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: JK Defence & Aerospace, a wholly owned subsidiary, is developing an Ultra Modern 400,000 sq ft advanced manufacturing complex at Devanahalli (North Bengaluru) for precision-turned components, systems and sub-systems for defence and aerospace: 200,000 sq ft precision manufacturing, a 100,000 sq ft Additive Manufacturing Center able to house 80-100 industrial 3D metal printers, about 50,000 sq ft of R&D and the balance offices. Civil construction is expected by December 2026 and project completion in Q4, 2027; a Rights Issue is underway primarily to fund it, and the project scope includes repaying interim loans taken by JK Defence for the facility. The Company funded JK Defence and JK Digital through subscriptions to 0.1% OCRPS during FY26 and the current year. In FY26 the Cherlapally (Hyderabad) facility expansion was completed, adding capability for large composite structures and advanced underwater systems, and the Peenya orthopaedic implant manufacturing project was completed, received CDSCO MD13 certification and began trial production. In April 2026 the Company acquired the Patange Industries business undertaking (defence precision manufacturing, fabrication and engineering design) by slump sale. JK Defence raised its stake in Allen Reinforced Plastics from 76.41% to 92.92% by paying call monies on rights shares, and the Company raised its stake in J K Technosoft to 99.07% (fully-converted basis) through a share swap.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- customer lock-in: qualified supplier to strategic missile programmes, where vendor qualification limits substitution — evidence: AR states JKE 'significantly contributed to strategic missile programs through the provision of machined components and subassemblies' and in FY26 secured orders from BrahMos Aerospace, Bharat Dynamics, HAL, BARC, BEL, NSTL and ADA
- technology: proprietary Gen AI orchestration platform in the IT services arm — evidence: J K Technosoft's JIVA platform was deployed during FY26 for large enterprise customers across the United States and Europe
- scale: large additive-manufacturing footprint — evidence: Devanahalli complex planned at 400,000 sq ft with a 100,000 sq ft Additive Manufacturing Center able to house 80-100 industrial 3D metal printers; civil construction expected by December 2026 [planned]

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- MD&A flags high dependence on Government/Defence contracts, policies and budgetary allocations, and SWOT lists dependence on Government and institutional customers as a threat; adverse sectoral developments could impair business sustainability.
- MD&A Risks & Concerns cites intense competition from domestic and international players.
- Rapid technological advancements, including Artificial Intelligence, require continuous investment in technology and skills; directly relevant to the Digital Services business.
- SWOT weakness: production-related challenges, particularly in availability and retention of skilled technical workforce.
- SWOT weakness: capital-intensive nature of certain businesses requiring higher working capital and funding for growth.
- SWOT weakness: limited presence in export markets, concentrating the business on the domestic market.
- Adverse geopolitical, economic and regulatory conditions and disruptions in global supply chains may impact business and financial performance.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Evolve from a component supplier into a high-value, technology-driven manufacturing and solutions company for Defence, Aerospace, Orthopaedic Implants and Additive Manufacturing.
- Complete the Devanahalli precision manufacturing project and deepen the Defence & Aerospace business.
- Expand defence presence through acquisition: Patange Industries business undertaking (warheads, bulkheads, shells, complex engineering structures) bought on a slump sale basis.
- Qualify additive-manufactured defence products under Atmanirbhar Bharat; these are in final stages of qualification and approval for strategic applications.
- Grow the medical implants business (patient-specific, hip, spinal implants) and spread its distribution and market reach; collaboration with NEL-AIIMS on neurosurgical instruments via metal 3D printing and precision machining.
- Deepen customer focus in Digital Services around the JIVA AI orchestration platform and GenAI / Agentic AI solutions, and explore JIVA applications in the Defence and Aerospace ecosystem.
- Establish defence production on a 4.9 hectare industrial land parcel allotted by UPEIDA under the Defence Industrial Corridor, Lucknow Node.
- Consolidate control of key subsidiaries: stake in J K Technosoft raised to 99.07% (fully-converted basis) and JK Defence's stake in Allen raised from 76.41% to 92.92%.
